title: Philadelphia Fed Real-Time Data Research Center (Survey of Professional Forecasters, Greenbook/Tealbook, Livingston Survey, Real-Time Data Set)
questions: what do professional forecasters expect for real GDP growth this year and next
median SPF forecast for unemployment and CPI inflation over the next four quarters
10-year inflation expectations of professional forecasters over time
how far apart are forecasters (dispersion) on next year's GDP growth
Fed staff Greenbook forecasts of inflation in 2008
real GDP as it was first published, by vintage

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser; it downloads the Philadelphia Fed's .xlsx workbook. Upload the workbook unchanged (the pack reads the worksheet named in the spec). Without the links: SPF median and mean forecasts at https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/median-forecasts and .../mean-forecasts, dispersion at .../dispersion-forecasts, probabilities at .../probability-variables, Greenbook/Tealbook at .../greenbook, Livingston at .../livingston-historical-data, real-time data at .../real-time-data-set-full-time-series-history (each page lists the files).

cache.why: Workbooks change once a quarter (SPF) or less often; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: Published openly by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia; its online terms of use allow informational, educational and research use, with the Bank credited as the source. The Bank is not a federal agency, so the data are not public domain: credit it and do not imply its endorsement.

citation: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Real-Time Data Research Center, {dataset}, philadelphiafed.org, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which growth measure: quarter-over-quarter annualized (the SPF quarterly forecasts), annual-average over annual-average (SPF and Livingston annual GDP), or fourth-quarter over fourth-quarter (SPF annual CPI and PCE inflation)? Default: the measure the SPF release itself reports for that variable, named in the answer.
Median or mean across forecasters? Default: median, as in the SPF news release.
Which survey: the latest (default) or the one in force at a past date (each row is one survey)?
